evidence: coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:2419-2423 calls process_pre_bridge_control_result(...).await from that same function when result is None and a terminal error exists; cargo test reports error[E0733].
findings.impact: Every focused and full coop-sidecar build/test command fails with Rust E0733 before the control-terminal behavior can run, so the candidate is not buildable or certifiable.
findings.observation: The staged server.rs cannot compile: the async process_pre_bridge_control_result function awaits itself recursively in its None branch without boxing or another indirection.
findings.recommendation: Replace the self-await with an iterative/local terminal-error dispatch or introduce explicit boxed indirection, then rerun the required sidecar suite and lint checks.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:644-646 implements failure_receiver() with watch::Sender::subscribe(), while coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:829-848 publishes failed=true and send_replace(true); a receiver subscribed after that send considers the current version seen and its changed() branch waits for a future send.
coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:2925-2928 is the only idle-loop wake branch for writer failure, so the missing post-registration recheck leaves no independent wake path.
findings.impact: If the sole writer records failure between the precheck and failure_receiver subscription, the new watch receiver starts at the already-published version and changed() waits for a later update that never comes; an idle serving loop can remain alive without terminating the failed bridge.
findings.observation: The active session checks writer failure and only then subscribes a fresh watch receiver, with no state recheck after registration.
findings.recommendation: Register the durable failure receiver before the precheck and recheck the state after registration, or use a single retained receiver with an explicit post-registration state check; add a barrier-controlled idle-session regression.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:853-861 BridgeWriter::Drop calls task.abort() but never awaits the JoinHandle.
coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:1269-1274 BridgeIo::Drop only aborts the bridge reader task and relies on field Drop for BridgeWriter, so it also has no writer join.

coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:2266-2270 propagates reacquire_control_with_bridge errors with ?, leaving the local bridge Option populated; coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:2839-2855 has error returns that reach this path.
findings.impact: On an acquisition/recovery error, the function can return before the sole writer task has been awaited. A concurrently running actor may retain the socket or drain a buffered lifecycle request after the session has classified the bridge as terminal, violating the required joined teardown and no-stale-replay guarantee.
findings.observation: BridgeWriter shutdown joins its task only through the explicit async shutdown path; the BridgeWriter and BridgeIo Drop implementations merely abort handles, and pre-active bridge recovery can propagate errors while a BridgeIo still owns the writer.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every error/overflow/recovery exit that still owns BridgeIo awaits an explicit writer shutdown (or an equivalent abort-and-await helper) before returning; retain no writer task in a Drop-only path.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:5132-5163 sends one remote_update_command, comments that the peer is unread, and waits only for the shutdown ACK; no writer gate, in_flight assertion, or task-termination proof is present.
coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/server.rs:4697-4705 shows the deterministic blocked writer fixture exists only for direct BridgeWriter unit tests, not for the serving-loop regression.
findings.impact: The test can pass with the operating-system send buffer accepting the frame, so it does not deterministically exercise writer timeout, poison, or shutdown starvation and cannot catch a regression in the required real-path bound.
findings.observation: The real serving-path stalled_presence_bridge_write_does_not_delay_shutdown_ack test sends one small lifecycle frame and simply leaves the TCP peer unread; it never proves the sole writer is pending or in_flight, unlike the separate unit-only blocked writer fixture.
findings.recommendation: Add a server-owned test gate/barrier that proves the lifecycle write is in flight before issuing shutdown, then assert both the bounded ACK and writer-task termination on the real serving path.
